args.text:
Batch: 8 runs, all 8 accepted. 0 flagged, 8 cleared (r01–r08).
Checks: every run passes rigid-body invariance and closure. All 8 runs report the width-free ratio instead of assuming constant width, so the plane-sections check was not run. Its values are above threshold, which is expected when root width changes.
Profiles: the strain-rate (REGR) peak is at 421 µm from the tip in every run, and growth zones are 684–695 µm long. Apart from r01, centre REGR peaks fall between 52.96 and 53.15 %/h, so the large z-scores come from a near-zero batch spread, not from real differences.
r01: its REGR peak (111.5 %/h) and flank difference (-7.97 %/h) are both about 2.1 times r05's. Its settings, frame stride (time base) and final checks match r05's, and so does its profile shape: peak position, growth-zone length, flank-difference position and flank-to-REGR ratio. Read as a faster-growing root, not a measurement fault. One point is still open: r01's largest width-free ratio (-0.268 at 850 µm) is far outside the rest of the batch (-0.034 to 0.074). It doesn't change the decision, but someone should look at it.
Flagged runs share nothing, since none were flagged.
